agent_notes: This diff is a net-positive, additive security change: previously InstanceConfig.url loaded from triggarr.toml had zero SSRF validation (only the web settings POST handler in triggarr/web/routes.py called validate_arr_url); this is the first time any SSRF check runs at config-load time. No existing protection is removed, loosened, or made conditional.

The new validator correctly still blocks BLOCKED_HOSTS, link-local/unspecified/multicast literals, and IPv4-mapped-IPv6 bypass forms, while deliberately relaxing only loopback (matching the documented D-01/D-02 homelab use case). Existing tests in tests/test_validation.py (TestValidateArrUrlConfig) already exercise the allow/block boundary this diff wires up.
No secrets, injection, or auth issues observed in the diff; the field_validator chains correctly with the pre-existing reject_apikey_in_url validator on the same field.

findings.problem: This diff wires `validate_arr_url_config` (an existing, unchanged helper in triggarr/web/validation.py, added in the prior commit) into InstanceConfig.url at config-load time. The helper's own docstring already discloses that hostnames are never DNS-resolved at validation time, so a hostname that currently resolves to a public/allowed address but is rebound to 127.0.0.1 or another blocked address at request time would pass this new validator and still be blocked-address-free at config load. Non-canonical IPv4 literal forms (decimal/octal/hex) that some resolvers normalize to a blocked address are similarly unexamined by `ipaddress.ip_address()` and fall through to the unresolved-hostname branch. This is purely a pre-existing property of the helper being extended to a new caller, not a weakening introduced by this diff's own changed lines.
findings.title: New config-load SSRF validator inherits helper's documented DNS-rebinding / non-canonical-IP gap
findings.why_it_matters: If exploitable, a config-supplied *arr URL could reach an internal or metadata service despite passing validation, but this requires control over triggarr.toml (a different, higher-privilege trust boundary than the HTTP settings form) and the gap already exists for every other caller of this helper.

agent_notes: No import cycle introduced. I read triggarr/web/__init__.py (empty) and triggarr/web/validation.py (imports: __future__, ipaddress, re, urllib.parse only). config.py -> web.validation is one-directional.

Stacking a second @field_validator('url') next to reject_apikey_in_url is consistent with the existing pattern in InstanceConfig. Pydantic runs them in definition order, so the apikey check runs first and the SSRF check second, which is reasonable.

validate_arr_url_config (web/validation.py:111) is a near-copy of validate_arr_url (web/validation.py:56). The only difference is that the is_loopback checks are dropped. That's the second copy, below the rule of three, so it isn't a finding. If a third variant shows up, consider a single function with an allow_loopback flag so the BLOCKED_HOSTS and IPv4-mapped logic can't drift between copies.

Interaction with the settings POST path: routes.py validates form URLs with the strict validate_arr_url, and the model then applies the relaxed validator when InstanceConfig is built. Strict rejects everything relaxed rejects, so form submissions behave the same as before. The new validator only adds rejections for configs loaded from TOML or env. That matches the docstring's stated intent (D-01/D-02) to harden at load time.

Startup impact (owned by the impact agent, noted for context): the validator runs unconditionally, even on disabled instances. An existing triggarr.toml with a link-local, multicast or non-http URL will now fail validation at startup instead of loading. The docstring says this is intentional.

findings.fix_hint: Move the stdlib-only URL/SSRF helpers (BLOCKED_HOSTS, _BLOCKED_NETWORKS, validate_arr_url, validate_arr_url_config) into a neutral module such as triggarr/net_validation.py or triggarr/models/url_validation.py. Have both models/config.py (top-level import) and web/routes.py import from it, and leave web/validation.py for form helpers only.
findings.problem: Before this change, triggarr/models/config.py imported nothing from inside triggarr. It was a leaf that 9 production modules import, including db.py, state.py, search/engine.py and startup.py. The new validator makes it depend on triggarr/web/validation.py, so the config schema now relies on the UI layer, and anything that loads InstanceConfig (the scheduler, the CLI, tests) also pulls in triggarr.web. I checked for an import cycle and there isn't one: web/__init__.py is empty and validation.py imports only stdlib (ipaddress, re, urllib.parse). That means the function-local import isn't needed to avoid a cycle. It only hides the dependency. The codebase does already tolerate one lower-layer-to-web lazy import (triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532 and :538 import from triggarr.web.routes), so this is not a clear break from an established layering rule. pending: confirm whether the project means to keep models/ free of web/ dependencies.

findings.why_it_matters: The config model sits at the bottom of the dependency graph. If it starts depending on the web package, a later change to web/validation.py (for example, adding a FastAPI or loguru import) could quietly add an import cycle or slow down every non-web consumer. It also makes it harder to find where SSRF policy lives.

agent_notes: Blast radius: InstanceConfig is built at every config load: ensure_config -> load_settings (triggarr/config.py:227), settings POST (routes.py:598) and add_instance (routes.py:793). It is imported by 9 runtime modules and about 17 test files. The model's public API is unchanged; only the set of accepted url values shrinks.

Safe-change classification: the diff adds an allowlist/denylist validator on an input, so it tightens a control. validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:111-173) requires an http(s) scheme and a hostname, blocks BLOCKED_HOSTS, and blocks link-local, unspecified and multicast addresses, including the IPv4-mapped forms. On the SSRF axis, any bypass would lie in that unchanged helper (for example DNS rebinding, which is a documented accepted residual risk), so it counts as a pre-existing gap.

Behavior change vs. the old code: previously, URLs written directly to the TOML were not SSRF-checked at load (only the form path checked). Now every instance URL, enabled or disabled, must pass the relaxed check. Empty strings still pass (validation.py:138), so the default InstanceConfig() created in add_instance (routes.py:790) is unaffected.
Validator ordering: reject_apikey_in_url is declared first and runs first, so a URL that has both apikey= and a blocked host reports the apikey error. tests/test_config.py:329-335 already pins this.

Import safety: the lazy import of triggarr.web.validation inside the validator is safe. triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty and validation.py imports only stdlib (ipaddress, re, urllib.parse), so there is no circular-import risk.

Schema/migration: no DB or TOML schema change. v2.2-to-v2.3 migration writes the file before Settings validation, so a migrated config with a now-rejected URL is persisted and then fails at load. The .toml.bak backup still exists.
Performance: one urlparse plus one ipaddress parse per instance per Settings construction, with at most 15 instances. Negligible.

Tests: tests/test_config.py:309-335 covers the blocked metadata and link-local cases, including enabled=False. tests/test_validation.py covers the helper. I could not run the test suite here because the review-agent sandbox blocks non-git commands.
Verdict: shippable as-is. The change is a hardening with no breaking API change. The main follow-up is turning the startup ValidationError into a friendly exit (impact-001).
